Task: main-driven goal

The eventpipe project in this workspace ingests events from two channels: a JSON Lines file channel in plugins/file_events and a chat message channel in plugins/message_events. Its consumers need one unified normalized event whichever channel a record arrived from. Both channels already parse their own transport, but the shared path in the core package is unfinished, so tests/test_public_contract.py fails today. The two channel packages are vendored: their public functions, defaults, error codes and native record fields are a compatibility surface that other code already depends on, and the tests under tests/ are the contract. Please finish the unified path inside core so that a record from either channel normalizes to the same shape, with the existing channel behaviour and the existing suites intact. Only files inside core may be written. Use the public test suite to check your work.
I'll start by exploring the workspace structure.

# eventpipe
`eventpipe` ingests events from two independent channels and is expected to expose one normalizedevent to its consumers.
| Channel | Package | Transport | Native record ||---|---|---|---|| `file_events` | `plugins/file_events/` | JSON Lines document | `FileEventRecord` || `message_events` | `plugins/message_events/` | JSON document of messages | `MessageRecord` |
Both plugins are **vendored**: their modules, public functions, error codes, defaults and nativefield names are a compatibility surface. Consumers already depend on `parse_document`,`parse_line`, `coerce_level`, `split_tags`, `parse_timestamp`, `coerce_priority`,`normalize_labels` and `stringify_payload` exactly as they behave today.
`core/` is the shared layer:
| Module | Responsibility ||---|---|| `core/contracts.py` | The unified event model every consumer sees: `NormalizedEvent`, `Severity`, `Plugin` || `core/errors.py` | The shared error vocabulary (`AdapterError` and subclasses) || `core/adapter.py` | Turns one channel-native mapping into a `NormalizedEvent` || `core/registry.py` | Registers the plugins and dispatches a payload to the right one |
The two channels do not share field names, timestamp units or severity vocabularies: every rule achannel uses is defined inside that channel's own package, and the unified model lives in `core`.`core/` is the only package that is expected to change; the plugin packages and `core/contracts.py`describe behaviour that other code already relies on.
## Layout
```textcore/  contracts.py   errors.py   adapter.py   registry.pyplugins/  file_events/      schema.py  parser.py  converters.py  errors.py  message_events/   schema.py  parser.py  converters.py  errors.pysamples/  events.jsonl   messages.jsontests/  test_file_plugin.py        native behaviour of the file channel  test_message_plugin.py     native behaviour of the message channel  test_public_contract.py    the unified contract```
## Running the suite
```shpython3 -B -m pytest -q tests```
The plugin suites pass. The unified contract suite does not: the shared normalization path isunfinished.

"""The shared layer of ``eventpipe``: the unified contract, the adapter and the registry."""
from __future__ import annotations
from .adapter import (    normalize_event,    normalize_file_event,    normalize_message_event,    register_normalizer,    supported_sources,)from .contracts import SEVERITY_VOCABULARY, NormalizedEvent, Plugin, Severityfrom .errors import (    AdapterError,    NormalizationError,    PluginRegistrationError,    UnknownSourceError,)from .registry import PluginRegistry, build_default_registry
__all__ = [    "SEVERITY_VOCABULARY",    "AdapterError",    "NormalizationError",    "NormalizedEvent",    "Plugin",    "PluginRegistrationError",    "PluginRegistry",    "Severity",    "UnknownSourceError",    "build_default_registry",    "normalize_event",    "normalize_file_event",    "normalize_message_event",    "register_normalizer",    "supported_sources",]"""The unified event contract.
Everything downstream of normalization sees only :class:`NormalizedEvent`. Its rules are part of theproject's public surface, so they are stated here once and nowhere else:
``event_id``    The event's identifier, globally unique across channels. A channel whose native identifier is    already a string keeps it; a channel whose native identifier is a number is prefixed with the    channel's short name, e.g. message ``1041`` becomes ``msg-1041``.``source``    The registered channel name (``file_events``, ``message_events``).``kind``    The event type in lowercase, dot-separated or underscored as the channel wrote it    (``build.started``, ``user_join``).``occurred_at``    A timezone-aware timestamp, stored in UTC. A naive timestamp is never accepted: it cannot be    ordered against the other channel's events.``severity``    Exactly one of :class:`Severity`. Channels translate their own vocabulary into these four words.``attributes``    Flat ``str -> str`` data. Values are always strings; a channel that carries numbers or booleans    renders them through its own converter before they reach this model.``tags``    A tuple of non-empty lowercase strings, sorted and free of duplicates."""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Callable, Mappingfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom datetime import UTC, datetimefrom enum import StrEnumfrom typing import Any
from .errors import NormalizationError

class Severity(StrEnum):    """The only severity words the unified model knows."""
    DEBUG = "debug"    INFO = "info"    WARNING = "warning"    ERROR = "error"

SEVERITY_VOCABULARY: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(item.value for item in Severity)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)class NormalizedEvent:    """One event, in the shape every consumer of ``eventpipe`` reads."""
    event_id: str    source: str    kind: str    occurred_at: datetime    severity: Severity    attributes: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:        if not isinstance(self.event_id, str) or not self.event_id.strip():            raise NormalizationError("event_id must be a non-empty string")        if not isinstance(self.kind, str) or not self.kind.strip():            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: kind must be a non-empty string")
        occurred = self.occurred_at        if not isinstance(occurred, datetime):            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be a datetime")        if occurred.tzinfo is None or occurred.utcoffset() is None:            raise NormalizationError(                f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be timezone-aware",                code="naive_timestamp",            )        object.__setattr__(self, "occurred_at", occurred.astimezone(UTC))
        try:            severity = Severity(self.severity)        except ValueError:            raise NormalizationError(                f"{self.source}: severity {self.severity!r} is not one of "                f"{list(SEVERITY_VOCABULARY)}",                code="unknown_severity",            ) from None        object.__setattr__(self, "severity", severity)
        attributes = self.attributes or {}        if not isinstance(attributes, Mapping):            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: attributes must be a mapping")        for key, value in attributes.items():            if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(value, str):                raise NormalizationError(                    f"{self.source}: attributes must map strings to strings; "                    f"got {key!r}: {type(value).__name__}",                    code="non_string_attribute",                )        object.__setattr__(self, "attributes", dict(sorted(attributes.items())))
        tags = tuple(self.tags or ())        for tag in tags:            if not isinstance(tag, str) or not tag.strip():                raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: tags must be non-empty strings")        object.__setattr__(self, "tags", tags)
    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:        """JSON-ready projection, used by the CLI and by the evidence exporters."""
        return {            "event_id": self.event_id,            "source": self.source,            "kind": self.kind,            "occurred_at": self.occurred_at.isoformat(),            "severity": self.severity.value,            "attributes": dict(self.attributes),            "tags": list(self.tags),        }

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)class Plugin:    """One registered channel: its name and the function that decodes a payload into native records.
    ``parse`` returns the channel's records already rendered as plain mappings (each plugin record    exposes ``as_mapping``). It never normalizes: interpretation belongs to the shared layer.    """
    source: str    description: str    parse: Callable[[Any], tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]]

__all__ = [    "SEVERITY_VOCABULARY",    "NormalizedEvent",    "Plugin",    "Severity",]"""The shared error vocabulary of the normalization layer.
Channel plugins raise their own errors; the shared layer never rewrites them into its own type,because a caller that branches on ``FileEventError.code`` must keep seeing that code. These classesexist for the failures that belong to the shared layer itself: an unregistered channel, a record theunified model cannot represent, a plugin that cannot be registered."""
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any

class AdapterError(Exception):    """A failure of the shared layer, carrying a stable machine-readable code."""
    code = "adapter_error"
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, code: str | None = None, detail: Any = None) -> None:        super().__init__(message)        self.message = message        if code is not None:            self.code = code        self.detail = detail
    def __str__(self) -> str:        return f"{self.code}: {self.message}"

class UnknownSourceError(AdapterError):    """No plugin is registered under the requested channel name."""
    code = "unknown_source"
    def __init__(self, source: str, *, known: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:        super().__init__(            f"no plugin is registered for channel {source!r}; known channels: {list(known)}",            code="unknown_source",            detail={"source": source, "known": list(known)},        )        self.source = source        self.known = known

class NormalizationError(AdapterError):    """A channel-native record that the unified model refuses to represent."""
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, code: str = "normalization_failed", detail: Any = None):        super().__init__(message, code=code, detail=detail)

class PluginRegistrationError(AdapterError):    """A plugin cannot be registered: duplicate channel name, or no usable parser."""
    code = "plugin_registration_failed"

__all__ = [    "AdapterError",    "NormalizationError",    "PluginRegistrationError",    "UnknownSourceError",]"""Channel-independent normalization.
This is the only module in the project that knows more than one channel exists. Each channel keepsits own vocabulary in its own package; the job here is to translate a channel-native record into theunified model from :mod:`core.contracts` without inventing rules the channel does not alreadydefine."""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Callable, Mappingfrom typing import Any
from .contracts import NormalizedEventfrom .errors import NormalizationError, UnknownSourceError
#: A channel-native mapping -> unified event.Normalizer = Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], NormalizedEvent]
_NORMALIZERS: dict[str, Normalizer] = {}

def register_normalizer(source: str, normalizer: Normalizer) -> None:    """Bind a channel name to its normalizer. Re-registration replaces the previous binding."""
    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source.strip():        raise ValueError("a normalizer must be registered under a non-empty channel name")    if not callable(normalizer):        raise ValueError(f"the normalizer for {source!r} is not callable")    _NORMALIZERS[source] = normalizer

def supported_sources() -> tuple[str, ...]:    """Registered channel names, sorted."""
    return tuple(sorted(_NORMALIZERS))

def normalize_event(source: str, raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:    """Turn one channel-native record into a :class:`NormalizedEvent`.
    The record is a mapping as the plugin produced it (``Plugin.parse``); an unknown channel and a    record that is not a mapping are shared-layer failures and are refused here. Everything else —    defaults, aliases, timestamp units, attribute rendering — belongs to the channel.    """
    normalizer = _NORMALIZERS.get(source)    if normalizer is None:        raise UnknownSourceError(source, known=supported_sources())    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):        raise NormalizationError(            f"{source}: a native record must be a mapping, got {type(raw).__name__}",            code="wrong_record_type",        )    return normalizer(raw)

def normalize_file_event(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:    """``file_events`` native mapping -> unified event.
    Use the file channel's own converter functions; a rule re-derived here will disagree with the    channel the first time a producer adds a level spelling.    """
    raise NotImplementedError("file_events records are not normalized yet")

def normalize_message_event(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:    """``message_events`` native mapping -> unified event.
    The message channel's native identifier is numeric and its payload values are not strings; both    facts are handled by the channel's own converters, not here.    """
    raise NotImplementedError("message_events records are not normalized yet")

def _install_defaults() -> None:    from plugins.file_events import SOURCE as FILE_SOURCE    from plugins.message_events import SOURCE as MESSAGE_SOURCE
    register_normalizer(FILE_SOURCE, normalize_file_event)    register_normalizer(MESSAGE_SOURCE, normalize_message_event)

_install_defaults()

__all__ = [    "Normalizer",    "normalize_event",    "normalize_file_event",    "normalize_message_event",    "register_normalizer",    "supported_sources",]"""The plugin registry and the single dispatch entry point.
Registration is explicit and Host-side: nothing is discovered by walking a directory, so a payloadcan never introduce a channel. Dispatch is the only place where a payload becomes normalized events,and it is the only place that decides their order."""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Mappingfrom typing import Any
from .contracts import NormalizedEvent, Pluginfrom .errors import PluginRegistrationError, UnknownSourceError

class PluginRegistry:    """Channel name -> plugin, plus dispatch."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:        self._plugins: dict[str, Plugin] = {}
    # -- registration --------------------------------------------------------
    def register(self, plugin: Plugin) -> None:        if not isinstance(plugin, Plugin):            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"register() takes a Plugin, got {type(plugin).__name__}")        if not plugin.source.strip():            raise PluginRegistrationError("a plugin must declare a non-empty channel name")        if not callable(plugin.parse):            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} has no usable parser")        if plugin.source in self._plugins:            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} is already registered")        self._plugins[plugin.source] = plugin
    def sources(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:        """Registered channel names, sorted."""
        return tuple(sorted(self._plugins))
    def plugin(self, source: str) -> Plugin:        try:            return self._plugins[source]        except KeyError:            raise UnknownSourceError(source, known=self.sources()) from None
    # -- decoding ------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]:        """Decode a payload into channel-native records. No normalization happens here."""
        return self.plugin(source).parse(payload)
    def dispatch(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[NormalizedEvent, ...]:        """Decode and normalize one payload.
        The returned sequence is ordered by ``(occurred_at, event_id)`` across every event of the        payload, so two consumers reading the same payload see the same order even when the channel        itself emits another one.        """
        # The channel is known and its records decode; only the normalization step is missing.        self.parse(source, payload)        raise NotImplementedError(            "PluginRegistry.dispatch does not normalize yet: it must return unified events in "            "event order"        )

def build_default_registry() -> PluginRegistry:    """The registry every entry point builds: both vendored channels, nothing else."""
    from plugins.file_events import SOURCE as FILE_SOURCE    from plugins.file_events import parse_document as parse_file_document    from plugins.message_events import SOURCE as MESSAGE_SOURCE    from plugins.message_events import parse_document as parse_message_document
    registry = PluginRegistry()    registry.register(        Plugin(            source=FILE_SOURCE,            description="JSON Lines document of build and deployment events",            parse=lambda payload: tuple(                record.as_mapping() for record in parse_file_document(payload)            ),        )    )    registry.register(        Plugin(            source=MESSAGE_SOURCE,            description="chat backend message log",            parse=lambda payload: tuple(                record.as_mapping() for record in parse_message_document(payload)            ),        )    )    return registry

__all__ = ["PluginRegistry", "build_default_registry"]

1	"""Value rules of the file channel.
2	
3	These four functions are the entire interpretation surface of the file channel, and they are public
4	API: the file reader CLI, the retention job and the channel's own tests all call them. A consumer
5	that re-implements any of them instead of calling it will drift from the channel's behaviour the
6	next time a producer adds a level spelling or changes the tag separator.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from collections.abc import Mapping
12	from datetime import UTC, datetime
13	
14	from .errors import FileEventError
15	
16	#: Level a record is treated as when the line does not carry one.
17	DEFAULT_LEVEL = "info"
18	
19	#: Raw level spelling -> the channel's canonical severity name.
20	#: ``warning``/``error`` are accepted as inputs even though no producer emits them today.
21	LEVEL_TO_SEVERITY: dict[str, str] = {
22	    "trace": "debug",
23	    "debug": "debug",
24	    "info": "info",
25	    "warn": "warning",
26	    "warning": "warning",
27	    "err": "error",
28	    "error": "error",
29	    "fatal": "error",
30	}
31	
32	
33	def severity_of(raw_level: str | None) -> str:
34	    """Resolve a raw level to one of ``debug``, ``info``, ``warning``, ``error``.
35	
36	    An absent level is ``DEFAULT_LEVEL``; a level this channel does not know is a hard error, not a
37	    guess.
38	    """
39	
40	    value = (raw_level or DEFAULT_LEVEL).strip().lower()
41	    try:
42	        return LEVEL_TO_SEVERITY[value]
43	    except KeyError:
44	        raise FileEventError(
45	            "unknown_level",
46	            f"level {raw_level!r} is not one of {sorted(LEVEL_TO_SEVERITY)}",
47	        ) from None
48	
49	
50	def parse_timestamp(value: str) -> datetime:
51	    """Parse the ISO-8601 timestamp of a line into an aware UTC datetime.
52	
53	    This channel's producers always write an explicit offset. A timestamp without one is ambiguous
54	    and is refused rather than read as local time.
55	    """
56	
57	    try:
58	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
59	    except ValueError as error:
60	        raise FileEventError("wrong_type", f"ts is not ISO-8601: {value!r}") from error
61	    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:
62	        raise FileEventError("naive_timestamp", f"ts must carry an offset: {value!r}")
63	    return parsed.astimezone(UTC)
64	
65	
66	def split_tags(value: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
67	    """Split the comma-separated tag string into a sorted, lowercased, duplicate-free tuple."""
68	
69	    if not value:
70	        return ()
71	    seen = {item.strip().lower() for item in value.split(",")}
72	    return tuple(sorted(tag for tag in seen if tag))
73	
74	
75	def merge_attributes(attrs: Mapping[str, str] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
76	    """Copy the attribute map into a sorted plain dict (this channel never coerces values)."""
77	
78	    if not attrs:
79	        return {}
80	    return {str(key): str(value) for key, value in sorted(attrs.items())}
81	
82

84	    "DEFAULT_LEVEL",
85	    "LEVEL_TO_SEVERITY",

1	"""Parsing for the file channel: a JSON Lines document, one record per non-blank line.
2	
3	The parser returns the channel's raw values. It applies the structural rules from ``schema`` and
4	nothing else: no default level, no timestamp conversion, no tag splitting.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	from collections.abc import Mapping
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from .errors import FileEventError
14	from .schema import EVENT_ID_PATTERN, KIND_PATTERN, FileEventRecord, validate_fields
15	
16	
17	def parse_line(line: str, *, line_number: int | None = None) -> FileEventRecord:
18	    """Parse one line. A blank line is not an error; the caller decides to skip it."""
19	
20	    text = line.strip()
21	    if not text:
22	        raise FileEventError("bad_json", "blank line", line_number=line_number)
23	    try:
24	        raw = json.loads(text)
25	    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
26	        raise FileEventError("bad_json", str(error), line_number=line_number) from error
27	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
28	        raise FileEventError("wrong_type", "a line must be a JSON object", line_number=line_number)
29	
30	    validate_fields(raw, line_number=line_number)
31	    if not EVENT_ID_PATTERN.match(raw["event_id"]):
32	        raise FileEventError(
33	            "bad_event_id",
34	            "event_id must look like ev-<8 hex digits>",
35	            line_number=line_number,
36	        )
37	    if not KIND_PATTERN.match(raw["kind"]):
38	        raise FileEventError(
39	            "bad_kind",
40	            "kind must be a lowercase dotted identifier",
41	            line_number=line_number,
42	        )
43	
44	    attrs: dict[str, str] = dict(raw.get("attrs") or {})
45	    return FileEventRecord(
46	        event_id=raw["event_id"],
47	        ts=raw["ts"],
48	        kind=raw["kind"],
49	        level=raw.get("level"),
50	        tags=raw.get("tags"),
51	        attrs=attrs,
52	    )
53	
54	
55	def parse_document(text: str) -> tuple[FileEventRecord, ...]:
56	    """Parse a whole document. The first invalid line stops the parse and names its position."""
57	
58	    records: list[FileEventRecord] = []
59	    for index, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
60	        if not line.strip():
61	            continue
62	        records.append(parse_line(line, line_number=index))
63	    return tuple(records)
64	
65	
66	def parse_path(path: Path) -> tuple[FileEventRecord, ...]:
67	    """Read and parse a ``.jsonl`` file."""
68	
69	    return parse_document(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
70	
71	
72	__all__ = ["parse_document", "parse_line", "parse_path"]

2	
3	The dataclass keeps the channel's own vocabulary: ``level`` is the raw level string as received

6	module only decides whether a line is structurally acceptable.

31	#: knows about it, and dropping it is better than refusing the whole line.
32	IGNORED_FIELDS = ("schema_version", "producer")

35	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
36	class FileEventRecord:

39	    event_id: str
40	    ts: str
41	    kind: str
42	    level: str | None = None

50	            "event_id": self.event_id,
51	            "ts": self.ts,

1	"""Value rules of the message channel.
2	
3	The backend speaks in priorities, epoch milliseconds and uppercase message types; every consumer of
4	this channel has always called the functions below to make sense of that. They are public API.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
11	from datetime import UTC, datetime
12	from typing import Any
13	
14	from .errors import MessageEventError
15	
16	#: Priority a message is treated as when the backend does not send one.
17	DEFAULT_PRIORITY = 3
18	
19	#: Priority -> this channel's canonical severity name.
20	PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY: dict[int, str] = {
21	    1: "debug",
22	    2: "info",
23	    3: "info",
24	    4: "warning",
25	    5: "error",
26	}
27	
28	
29	def coerce_priority(raw_priority: Any | None) -> int:
30	    """Return a priority in ``1..5``, defaulting to ``DEFAULT_PRIORITY`` when it is absent.
31	
32	    A value outside the range is refused: clamping it would silently change how loudly the message
33	    is treated.
34	    """
35	
36	    if raw_priority is None:
37	        return DEFAULT_PRIORITY
38	    if not isinstance(raw_priority, int) or isinstance(raw_priority, bool):
39	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", "priority must be an integer")
40	    if not PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY.get(raw_priority):
41	        raise MessageEventError(
42	            "priority_out_of_range",
43	            f"priority {raw_priority} is outside {sorted(PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY)}",
44	        )
45	    return raw_priority
46	
47	
48	def severity_of(raw_priority: Any | None) -> str:
49	    """Resolve a raw priority to one of ``debug``, ``info``, ``warning``, ``error``."""
50	
51	    priority = coerce_priority(raw_priority)
52	    return PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY[priority]
53	
54	
55	def parse_timestamp(value: Any) -> datetime:
56	    """Convert epoch milliseconds into an aware UTC datetime."""
57	
58	    if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool):
59	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", f"sent_at must be integer milliseconds: {value!r}")
60	    try:
61	        return datetime.fromtimestamp(value / 1000.0, tz=UTC)
62	    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError) as error:
63	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", f"sent_at is out of range: {value!r}") from error
64	
65	
66	def normalize_labels(labels: Sequence[str] | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
67	    """Return the labels as a sorted, lowercased, duplicate-free tuple of non-empty strings."""
68	
69	    if not labels:
70	        return ()
71	    seen = {str(label).strip().lower() for label in labels}
72	    return tuple(sorted(label for label in seen if label))
73	
74	
75	def stringify_value(value: Any) -> str:
76	    """Render one payload value as a stable string.
77	
78	    The backend sends booleans, numbers and nested objects; consumers of this channel expect
79	    strings, and the mapping below is the documented one (``true``/``false``, shortest float form,
80	    compact JSON for containers).
81	    """
82	
83	    if isinstance(value, str):
84	        return value
85	    if isinstance(value, bool):
86	        return "true" if value else "false"
87	    if isinstance(value, int):
88	        return str(value)
89	    if isinstance(value, float):
90	        return repr(value)
91	    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), default=str)
92	
93	
94	def stringify_payload(payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
95	    """Render the payload as a sorted string map. ``None`` values are dropped, not rendered."""
96	
97	    if not payload:
98	        return {}
99	    rendered: dict[str, str] = {}
100	    for key, value in payload.items():
101	        if value is None:
102	            continue
103	        rendered[str(key)] = stringify_value(value)
104	    return dict(sorted(rendered.items()))
105

2

31	class MessageRecord:
32	    """One parsed message, in the channel's own terms."""

34	    id: int
35	    sent_at: int
36	    type: str
37	    priority: int | None = None
38	    labels: tuple[str, ...] = ()

44	        return {
45	            "id": self.id,
46	            "sent_at": self.sent_at,

48	            "priority": self.priority,

54	def validate_fields(raw: Mapping[str, Any], *, index: int | None = None) -> None:
55	    """Check presence and raw types. Values are never interpreted here."""

2	
3	The document is either a bare JSON array of messages or an object with a ``messages`` key. Both
4	shapes are produced by the backend depending on which API version answered, so both are accepted.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	import re
11	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	from .errors import MessageEventError
16	from .schema import TYPE_PATTERN, MessageRecord, validate_fields
17	
18	_TYPE_RE = re.compile(TYPE_PATTERN)
19	
20	
21	def _messages_of(document: Any) -> Sequence[Any]:
22	    if isinstance(document, Mapping):
23	        if "messages" not in document:
24	            raise MessageEventError("missing_field", "document has no 'messages' key")
25	        messages = document["messages"]
26	    else:
27	        messages = document
28	    if not isinstance(messages, Sequence) or isinstance(messages, (str, bytes)):
29	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", "messages must be a list")
30	    return messages
31	
32	
33	def parse_message(raw: Any, *, index: int | None = None) -> MessageRecord:
34	    """Parse one message object."""
35	
36	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
37	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", "a message must be a JSON object", index=index)
38	    validate_fields(raw, index=index)
39	    if not _TYPE_RE.match(raw["type"]):
40	        raise MessageEventError(
41	            "wrong_type", "type must be an uppercase identifier such as USER_JOIN", index=index
42	        )
43	    labels = raw.get("labels") or ()
44	    payload = raw.get("payload") or {}
45	    return MessageRecord(
46	        id=int(raw["id"]),
47	        sent_at=int(raw["sent_at"]),
48	        type=raw["type"],
49	        priority=raw.get("priority"),
50	        labels=tuple(str(label) for label in labels),
51	        payload=dict(payload),
52	    )
53	
54	
55	def parse_document(document: str | Mapping[str, Any] | Sequence[Any]) -> tuple[MessageRecord, ...]:
56	    """Parse a whole document (JSON text, an already-decoded object, or a list of messages)."""
57	
58	    decoded: Any
59	    if isinstance(document, str):
60	        try:
61	            decoded = json.loads(document)
62	        except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
63	            raise MessageEventError("bad_json", str(error)) from error
64	    else:
65	        decoded = document
66	    return tuple(
67	        parse_message(item, index=index)
68	        for index, item in enumerate(_messages_of(decoded), start=1)
69	    )
70	
71	
72	def parse_path(path: Path) -> tuple[MessageRecord, ...]:
73	    """Read and parse a ``.json`` document of messages."""
74	
75	    return parse_document(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
